To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PAc peptide motif, which is the multiple binding motif of the HLA‐ DR molecule (L‐RV‐K/A), was identified.
the multiple binding motif of the PAc(310–330) peptide was identified by the binding motif analysis of the peptide analogues, which were synthesized by the substitution of amino acids with glycine.
the multiple binding motif of the A‐peptide in S. mutans PAc was found in L–RV–K–A, and this could be useful for the development of peptide vaccine for dental care.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a peptide vaccine for the prevention of dental caries, which is the most common disease in the general human populations, by identifying the binding motif of HLA‐DR molecules with the A‐region peptide of the PAc protein.
the identification of the binding motif of PAc(316‐334) peptide to HLA‐DR molecules.
the identification of a peptide antigen that is useful for the development of an effective dental caris vaccine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PAc protein of S. mutans is a promising candidate for the design of a vaccine against dental caries.
the PAc A‐region peptide, PAc(316‐334), is a potential target of a peptide vaccine against S. mutans‐induced dental caries.
a peptide vaccine against dental caries could be designed by using the peptide motif identified in the PAc(315–334) region of the A‐unit of the S. mutans PAc molecule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the binding motif of PAc(316‐334) peptide with DRB1*0801, *1101 and *1401/1405 molecules, which are common HLA alleles in Japanese people, using synthetic peptides.
the PAc peptide vaccine for dental care would be effective for the general human population by using a multiple binding motif and a B‐cell epitopes.
we identified the peptide binding with HLA‐DR molecules (DRB8*0802, DR5*1101, DR6*1402, DR6*1415) in the A‐Region (316–334) of PAc, which is a surface protein antigen of S. mutans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peptide could therefore be a useful peptide for peptide vaccine development.
we have successfully identified a peptide motif binding with the human HLA‐DR molecules.
we can use a simple ELISA binding assay to identify peptide binding to HLA‐DR molecules.
